nodes.description: External pure function compute(uint256 x) that evaluates a high-degree polynomial (Pedersen hash Y column point precomputation) using inline assembly and returns result % PRIME.
Input parameter x, the evaluation point of the polynomial; multiplied repeatedly inside the assembly Horner loop.
Local constant PRIME = 0x800000000000011000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000001 used as the modulus for every mulmod operation and for the final reduction.
Inline assembly Horner evaluation performing chained add(mulmod(..., x, PRIME)) over dozens of hardcoded coefficients; arithmetic is unchecked and non-reverting inside assembly.

edges.reason: The function body unconditionally transfers control into the inline assembly block that computes the polynomial via Horner's method.
Parameter x flows directly into every mulmod(accumulator, x, PRIME) step of the assembly evaluation, so its value drives all unchecked modular multiplications.
The local PRIME constant is the modulus argument of every mulmod in the assembly and the divisor of the final result % PRIME reduction.
Parameter x is consumed by the function compute and returned as the reduced polynomial value.
PRIME is used outside the assembly for the final modulo reduction of result, affecting the returned value.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter x is only meaningful as the argument of the compute function and should be folded into that core function node.
Local constant PRIME exists solely to serve as the modulus of the assembly mulmod unsafe operation and is merged into it.
